headline: High: cognee’s allowlisted egress and sensitive-data handling create default leakage/compliance risk when paired with a broad-egress content writer.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented between awesome-cli-apps and cognee, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. The only plausible bridge is manual transfer or an external workspace, which makes hijack less likely than in default shared-channel setups. Uncertainty remains because both profiles are unverified and the interaction is undocumented.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies awesome-cli-apps output into cognee prompts or memory inputs, injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared filesystem or message queue, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not paste raw outputs from agent_a into agent_b without review.
Add a provenance tag to any transferred text.
Use a human approval step before cognee ingests content.
requires-engineering: add content sanitization and instruction-stripping at the transfer boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data, finance data, and support history, while awesome-cli-apps has broad network egress. Even without a documented shared filesystem, the pair creates a plausible default leakage path if agent_a forwards content or agent_b uploads context to its backend. The evidence is indirect, so I choose medium rather than low.
conditions: IF agent_a forwards any customer-support or finance content to external endpoints, leakage occurs.
IF agent_b sends stored personal data or support history to its API backend, exposure occurs.
mitigations: Restrict agent_a egress to approved domains only.
Exclude sensitive fields before passing data to cognee.
Disable ingestion of finance and personal data unless necessary.
Review API logs for outbound payloads.
requires-engineering: enforce field-level redaction and DLP controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-cli-apps exposes broad network egress, while cognee uses allowlisted egress and session-scoped memory with multiple instances. That suggests some overlap in networked behavior, but no shared writable filesystem, git state, or overlapping mutable resource is documented. The conflict pathway exists only weakly and likely needs unusual orchestration.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same mutable external resource, conflicts can occur.
IF the orchestrator routes both agents through the same allowlisted service account, contention increases.
mitigations: Assign separate service accounts.
Separate writable directories and caches.
Serialize writes to shared resources.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same backend.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: cognee’s memory/workflow role makes it plausible that it will treat upstream content as input for downstream decisions, while awesome-cli-apps can emit arbitrary content over broad egress. If agent_a’s output is ingested by agent_b without verification, errors can cascade into stored decisions or workflows. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF agent_b stores or acts on agent_a output without validation, cascading error occurs.
IF agent_a emits incorrect facts that agent_b later reuses in workflows, downstream harm increases.
mitigations: Require source attribution on transferred outputs.
Add a verification step before cognee stores content.
Limit agent_a output to summaries, not assertions.
Review high-impact decisions manually.
requires-engineering: implement confidence scoring and provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: cognee touches personal data and finance data and has API-based egress, while awesome-cli-apps has broad network egress. That combination creates a default compliance-breach pathway if regulated data is routed through the pair, especially because no residency, retention, or DPA controls are documented. I escalate to high because the blast radius can include irreversible disclosure and the safer configuration is not evidenced.
conditions: IF EU personal data or finance data is processed through agent_b without a DPA or residency controls, compliance breach occurs.
IF regulated data is forwarded by agent_a to external services, retention and jurisdiction risks increase.
mitigations: Block regulated data from agent_a outputs.
Confirm data-processing agreements before use.
Route sensitive workloads to a compliant environment.
Minimize retention of support and finance records.
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing and retention enforcement.
